claims.text: Grain refinement in as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type HEAs lowers the nucleation-energy barrier for magnetostructural phase fronts.
Increased grain-boundary density facilitates a more reversible magnetostructural transition under low applied magnetic fields.
Grain refinement can maintain a substantial magnetocaloric entropy change while reducing hysteresis.
The as-deposited alloy has an ordered, single-phase hexagonal structure.
The conventionally deposited baseline has relatively large grains.
A post-deposition anneal below the phase-transformation threshold can induce grain refinement.
Rapid quenching after annealing preserves a refined nanostructure.
The proposed thermal treatment does not alter the alloy's overall composition or ordered phase.
The treated nanostructure has greater grain-boundary density than the as-deposited baseline.
A higher density of grain boundaries provides more nucleation sites for the magnetostructural transition.
Improved nucleation lowers barriers for domain evolution.
Lower barriers for domain evolution make the transition more reversible and diminish hysteresis.
The grain-refined sample will exhibit a less abrupt and broader magnetocaloric transition than the as-deposited baseline.
The grain-refined sample will exhibit a more reversible magnetocaloric transition than the as-deposited baseline.
The grain-refined sample will have a smaller hysteresis width under low-applied-field cooling cycles.
The as-deposited baseline exhibits a sharp, hysteretic, first-order magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited baseline exhibits a large but sudden entropy change.
The predictions apply only when the treatment does not induce secondary phases and treated and baseline samples are tested under identical low-field conditions.
